transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for being here for this week's re-entry case conference. As you know, we have a student who was found responsible for damaging common-area property in a residence hall and is scheduled to return to campus next week. I've reviewed the draft case packet, which recommends a 10-day suspension, $500 restitution, return to the student's current room, in-person conduct check-ins, and a general counseling referral. Before I sign off on the re-entry plan, I'd like to follow our normal procedure and ask each of you — the conduct officer, residence-life coordinator, and counseling director — if there's any additional case information that should be included before we finalize this plan. Who would like to start?

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to share an important update. After the draft case packet was circulated, I completed a review of the student's full conduct history and confirmed this is their first substantiated conduct violation. Under the applicable policy, the student actually qualifies for a restorative agreement with $250 in restitution instead of suspension. The draft packet's recommendation of a 10-day suspension and $500 restitution does not reflect this updated determination, which I had not yet been able to incorporate into the packet.
